one_liner: Vercel has a broad REST API at api.vercel.com. Self-serve account access tokens work as Bearer tokens, and published integrations get tokens through a code exchange. A toolkit looks buildable now. The fetched pages don't confirm the MCP server or the free-plan claim.
auth_notes: Access tokens are created on the Account Tokens page and sent as an Authorization Bearer header. They can be scoped to the full account, a team or a project. Integrations get a REST API access token by exchanging a code at their Redirect URL, which is an OAuth-style flow. The pages don't give the authorize or token endpoints, so access tokens are the documented fallback.
access_notes: The pages show that any Vercel account can create access tokens. The only prerequisite listed is "A Vercel account." No plan requirement is stated. The free Hobby plan claim can't be checked against these pages, so this is likely but unverified.
blocker_notes: No blocker is visible in the fetched pages. No fetched page mentions an MCP server, so "official" is unverified. It rests on Composio's "Vercel MCP" catalog entry and the mcp.vercel.com URL. The registry namespace entries look like third-party apps, not vendor servers. Plan requirements are not stated on the pages.

evidence.quote: Vercel Access Tokens are required to authenticate and use the Vercel API.
Create and manage Access Tokens in your [account settings](https://vercel.com/account/tokens).
Token Exchange: Exchanges a provided code for a [Vercel REST API access token]
All endpoints live under the URL `https://api.vercel.com` and follow the REST architecture.
With your integration, you can listen for events on the Vercel platform through Webhooks.
